sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Christian Horner indicated in an interview that he would consider the Ferrari team principal role, prompting a public response from Frederic Vasseur. Meanwhile, George Russell won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after holding off Max Verstappen, and Formula 1 addressed questions regarding the end-of-season calendar and the handling of a late crash by Valtteri Bottas.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Horner's comments highlight speculation about his future, though his demand for overall control makes a move to Ferrari unlikely given their management structure. Furthermore, questions arose over whether race control should have deployed a safety car following the late crash in Baku.

quotes.text: Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1.
Mr Horner is looking for a job - that, everybody knows - everywhere.

sections.text: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua arrived in London ahead of a launch news conference in Olympia. The bout was announced for 11 December at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, but faced disputes over Dana White's promotional role and questions regarding Fury's anti-doping enrollment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The chaotic buildup highlighted recurring issues in boxing, overshadowing a lucrative shared purse and frustrating supporters who have waited years for the matchup.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The fighters are set to appear face-to-face at the Wednesday launch event in London, which could help shift the focus back to the sporting contest.

fivew: An all-British heavyweight boxing contest between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.
The fight was arranged following an announcement by Saudi powerbroker Turki Alalshikh.
